extracted.intended_audience: mathematics department faculty, department chairs, assessment coordinators, and university administrators involved in undergraduate curriculum and general-education assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and case studies on designing and using surveys, program metrics, departmental policies, and interunit collaboration to assess and improve quantitative literacy, developmental mathematics, and course delivery in undergraduate mathematics programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of pre/post-testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre/post-testing reveals what progress students have made but does not reveal what brought about that progress or what should be done to bring about greater progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre/post-test comparative data only reveals progress; it cannot disaggregate the contributions of specific interventions (e.g., journals, extra board work, homework). Detecting negative progress points to need for pedagogical change but does not provide the formula for improvement. Pre/post-testing must be accompanied by teacher creativity and flexibility in devising new techniques; the tool's value depends on how it is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: General education course approval — meet 3 of 5 criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: General education courses can only be approved if they meet three of the following five criteria: (1) basic academic skills (including mathematical skills), (2) awareness of interrelation among disciplines, (3) critical thinking, (4) values awareness, and (5) multicultural/gender awareness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course approval is conditional on satisfying at least three criteria; these program criteria form the basis for revalidation and survey question design used in assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student perception survey instrument (1–5 scale on program criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: A simple survey instrument asking students whether they were aware of opportunities to develop in the program criteria areas, with responses collected on a 1–5 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys were administered broadly across general education classes, coded onto scannable forms, processed centrally, and returned as data reports to departments. The survey data were intended to provide feedback to instructors, to inform departments during course revalidation, and to help the general education program trace operationality of program criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course revalidation requirement — report and reflect on survey data
rubrics_metrics.description: Revalidation of a general education course requires that survey data be reported and reflected upon as part of the application for continuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departments must include survey results in revalidation materials and use them to rationalize continuation or propose course changes (e.g., alternative readings, new assignments, software). Revalidation is on a five-year cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey instruments are formative and have limited validity/reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Student-perception surveys are instruments of fairly weak validity and reliability and are not instruments for measuring academic achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use survey results as a fuzzy snapshot or rhetorical/formative tool to generate discussion and point to issues; do not treat them as definitive measures of learning. Counterintuitive or anomalous results should prompt investigation for explanations rather than automatic judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative literacy definition and added basic skills
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'mathematical component' was rephrased as the 'quantitative literacy' component, redefined in terms of quantitative and formal thinking, and additional basic skills criteria were added relating to computer experience and science laboratory experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised program criteria should be reflected in new survey instruments. Early results suggested students perceived more mathematics across the curriculum after the requirement and criterion redefinition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use survey results to prompt curricular discussion and change
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey results should be used to generate faculty discussion about definitions and learning expectations and to prompt concrete curricular adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a sociology course scoring 3.8 with high variance and 25% 'not applicable' responses would trigger debate about what quantitative-thinking expectations are appropriate, potentially leading to adding alternative readings or statistical analysis assignments and changes in assessment within the course.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with institutional and accreditation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment activities should align with institutional/system expectations and accreditation requirements, which may require reporting student learning data to justify program expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faculty awareness that assessment reporting will be required long-term helps legitimize and motivate data collection; later revalidation cycles may require academic achievement data beyond perception surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key evaluation metrics for developmental mathematics programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Core metrics examined for developmental programs include retention/graduation rates, entrance category analysis, enrollment and grades in developmental and subsequent core courses, repeat rates for developmental courses, and correlations between developmental course performance and successful completion of core mathematics sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies analyzed cohorts over multiple years, comparing categories (regular admits, EOF, ESSP), SAT scores, GPA, and course grades. Findings showed strong correlation between developmental course grade and completion rates in core courses; these metrics drive program decisions and interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developmental-course grade → core-completion correlation (grading metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance in developmental courses strongly correlates with successful completion of core curriculum mathematics courses; higher developmental course grades predict higher rates of core completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported table (as findings) mapped developmental course grades to percentage completing core (e.g., 4.0 → 53%, 3.0–3.5 → 44%, 2.0–2.5 → 36%, 1.0–1.5 → 26%, 0.0 → 3%, WA/WD/IC → 2%, no developmental course → 60%). Use such mappings to target interventions and early identification of at-risk students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-to-completion metric for core mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure the percentage of entering freshmen who complete the core mathematics requirement within a target time (e.g., within two years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example finding: approximately 55% of entering freshmen completed the core mathematics requirement within two years. Use this metric to track program effectiveness over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome metric: post-core continuation/graduation
rubrics_metrics.description: Track the proportion of students who, after completing the core mathematics requirement, continue in their studies or graduate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example finding: for the cohorts studied, 86% of those who completed the core mathematics requirement were continuing or had graduated by the end of the reporting term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional interventions informed by assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use assessment findings to implement targeted instructional changes such as computer-supported learning modules, personalized instruction, graphing calculator use, tutoring centers, 'Writing to Learn' methods, and short preparatory academies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saint Peter’s and other departments introduced interventions (CALL, graphing calculators, writing-to-learn journals, Summer Academy) in response to data. Assessment should guide selection, piloting, and scaling of such interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success factors for developmental mathematics programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Key success ingredients include personal attention and support, peer tutoring, cooperative learning, encouragement from faculty and family, regular attendance, good study habits, and student persistence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs should prioritize early identification of 'at risk' students, provide tutoring and mentoring, and cultivate habits that support retention and progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unified departmental policy: clear goals and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a unified departmental policy stating goals (e.g., 'an academically sound curriculum in which most conscientious students could expect to be successful') and commitments (provide skills needed for later courses, consider changes to increase student success).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear, debated, and approved statement of departmental aims sets the context for assessment, course policy, and interactions with other units; it helps the department decide what it is trying to do, how it will measure success, and how to make changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of course policies across sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure consistent course policies (prerequisites, grading, calculator usage, syllabus, study habits suggestions) in all sections of a given course during a semester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student and Instructor Information Sheets distributed at the start of each course document these policies; consistency supports fairness and reliable assessment of course outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course documentation: Student and Instructor Information Sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain Student Information Sheets (prerequisites, grading, calculator usage, syllabus, study-habit suggestions) and Instructor Information Sheets (typical clientele, test-construction templates, current course issues, historical success rates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial approval of these sheets is by the department; future revisions are proposed by the course leader and approved by the undergraduate committee, ensuring transparency and continuity across instructors and semesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course development and revision process with assigned responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Allocate responsibilities for course development and continuing improvement between teaching faculty, designated course leaders, and the curriculum/undergraduate committee, with a process for proposing and approving changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This process institutionalizes assessment: course leaders initiate revisions, the curriculum committee reviews, and departmental approval is sought for major changes; this structure supports data-informed continuous improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: External consultation with client departments via liaisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage client academic units (e.g., natural sciences, engineering, computer science) by appointing faculty liaisons to consult on course content, text selection, and curricular reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liaisons are interviewed, invited to review materials, and participate in forums; such consultation builds support for changes (e.g., calculus reform) and can lead to permanent liaison roles or committee seats for client units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration with student-support units and resource sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Coordinate with units like the Academic Skills Center to provide peer tutoring, supplemental instruction, and study-skills seminars; faculty should participate in tutor training and may allocate office hours at the center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Departmental support (including funding and faculty engagement) for the Center's services is both pedagogically beneficial and visible to the institution; departments may subsidize or otherwise support tutoring beyond their own budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-driven responses to external task force recommendations (placement & content)
rubrics_metrics.description: When external units (e.g., business school) raise issues about placement or course content, respond with careful information gathering, commissioned studies, pilot projects, and joint-funded initiatives to inform formal departmental responses and course changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a task force on the pre-major mathematics sequence involved studies and pilots; the department developed formal responses and appointed liaisons to oversee implementation, demonstrating the importance of evidence-based decision making in curricular alignment and placement policies.
